status_summary: No program named or modeled as a clean standards initiative was found. America's AI Action Plan, released 2025-07-23, recommends that State and Commerce use U.S. influence in diplomatic and standard-setting bodies to promote innovation-friendly AI governance and counter authoritarian influence. On 2026-07-27 NTIA launched a non-binding Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, endorsed by 25 governments, under which participants intend to coordinate with industry to shape global 6G standards and promote strong security standards; the text does not name China or any vendor. Both steps are narrower than the comprehensive standards initiative the Mandate describes and neither excludes CCP-linked participants.

timeline.event: The White House released America's AI Action Plan, which recommends that State and Commerce use U.S. influence in diplomatic and standard-setting bodies to promote innovation-friendly AI governance and counter authoritarian influence.

NTIA launched the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, endorsed by 25 governments; participants intend to coordinate with industry on global 6G standards and security baselines, with milestones over 12 months. The text is non-binding and names no country or vendor.

title: Launch a clean standards initiative to counter CCP influence over technology standards
uncertainties: Five searches were run by the researcher on this item (State, Commerce and NIST standards actions; the State Department plan; FY2026 defense authorization provisions; a 6G initiative; the 6G call text). The NTIA press page does not mention standards or China; only the call document does, and the call is dated by the press release because the PDF prints no date. The Action Plan PDF prints only July 2025; the 2025-07-23 release date comes from a law-firm tracker dated that day. The State Department 2026-2030 plan could not be opened; its standards language comes from one trade article and is not counted as an event. A CRS note on cyber and AI provisions of the FY2026 defense authorization law showed no standards provision, but the full law was not searched. No NIST Federal Register notice on China and standards was found. The stage is a judgment: the Action Plan item is a recommendation and the 6G call is a voluntary statement of intent that does not target CCP influence, so proposed 15 with a partial match is used; in_progress 25 is defensible if the 6G call is read as the launch of an allied standards effort.
